rca_of_the_issue: Iter21 shipped two coupled fixes with independent RCAs. (1) TRUNCATION: server.py my_products() row builder loaded product_snapshots via .to_list(50000). On production 90D windows the snapshot count exceeded 50k, so Motor silently truncated — the (sku, store_id) pairs that ended up dropped were non-deterministic (Mongo cursor order isn't stable across queries). This produced the observed anti-monotonic Carnilove case (2 competitors at 7D but only 1 at 30D — the 30D pull happened to drop the second store's snapshots). Fix: replace the flat find+.to_list with a $group aggregation that pre-collapses to one document per (sku, store_id) carrying (min_price, max_price, latest_snapshot). Grouped doc count is bounded by distinct pairs (~35k) which is well under any hard limit and comfortably within Motor's default 100MB working set. Verified: monotonicity now holds strictly on Carnilove, Beaphar, and 5 random own-store SKUs. (2) PRICE RATIO: matcher.py Level-1 rejected barcode matches when price_ratio > 2.0×, Level-2 rejected SKU matches when ratio > 1.5×. Aggressive discounts (Carnilove 2.93 SAR vs 15 SAR market = 5.1× ratio) triggered false rejects even when the barcode was identical (definitive same-product evidence). Fix: remove the hard rejects; keep the informational SUSPICIOUS_PRICE flag but scope it to Level-2 (SKU) only, since barcode equality alone is enough to trust the match regardless of price gap. Verified: Carnilove now has 2 barcode matches at confidence=99 with no flags, and globally zero barcode matches in db.product_matches carry SUSPICIOUS_PRICE. Mitigation locked in by /app/backend/tests/test_iteration21_predeploy_api.py (24 tests) + the previously-added test_iteration21_truncation_and_ratio.py.
